title: Annotatio IV §.XXII close: Strimesius prefers posterior + crucified/shed; Philip of Hesse to Luther
pass_a_gloss: This POSTERIOR exposition I also judge the better, adding: The same body of Christ which was crucified for us, and the same blood which was poured out for us, are SPIRITUALLY present in the Supper and SPIRITUALLY received by us — nay even inasmuch as that was crucified and this poured out on the altar of the cross… This comes nearer both to Christ’s Institution words and to the nature of the thing… Whence further the most Illustrious Lutheran Prince Philip Landgrave of Hesse ingeniously collects thus in a Letter to Luther for the Zwinglians…: And since Christ, he writes, because He has a clarified body by which the Belly cannot be fed, can scarcely be eaten otherwise than by Believers and through faith; These things, I say, being so, your sentence seems to me harder and not necessary.
pass_b_english: Strimesius judges the posterior better: the same crucified body and poured blood are SPIRITUALLY present and SPIRITUALLY received — even as crucified and poured on the cross — nearer Institution and the thing’s nature.
Philip of Hesse to Luther for the Zwinglians: a clarified body the belly cannot feed can scarcely be eaten except by believers through faith — so the harder Lutheran sentence seems unnecessary.
source_text: POSTERIOREM hanc expositionem & ego potiorem arbitror, addens: Idem corpus Christi, quod pro nobis crucifixum est, & sanguinem eundem, qui pro nobis effusus est, in Cœna SPIRITUALITER præsentia esse & à nobis SPIRITUALITER accipi, imò etiam, quatenus tùm istud crucifixum, tum hic in ara crucis effusus est… tam verbis Institutionis Christi… quàm naturæ rei, propius accedit… Unde porrò… ingeniosè sic colligente Illustrissimo Principe Lutheranô, Philippo Hassiæ Landgravió, in Epistola ad Lutherum pro Zwinglianis…: Cumque Christus, scribit, quia clarifactum corpus habet, quo Venter cibari nequit, vix aliter manducari possit, quàm à Credentibus & per fidem; Hæc, inquam, cum ita se habeant, mihi sententia vestra videtur durior & non necessaria esse.
